newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda slams UN, unconcerned over Boutros-Ghali.
newsitem.headline: Uganda slams UN, unconcerned over Boutros-Ghali.

text.p: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has accused the United Nations of joining a "criminal circus of all sorts of charlatans" in Central Africa and said he was not concerned about the re-election of its secretary-general.
Museveni attacked the world body's record in Africa at a news conference at his presidency in Kampala late on Tuesday.
"The United Nations has not done anything tangible for Africa. It is not a serious organisation. We are not concerned about election of the secretary-general right now," he said.

The United States cast a veto on Tuesday against U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali's re-election, on the grounds that the United Nations needed someone more amenable to reform. The other 14 council members voted for him.
The council has agreed to give priority to another candidate from Africa to succeed the Egyptian diplomat.
Museveni accused the United Nations of conspiring to keep Rwandan Hutu refugees in Zaire.

"The recent voluntary return of refugees to Rwanda from Zaire was a big shame for the United Nations. All along, the U.N. had not actively supported any proposals that would lead to such a repatriation," Museveni told reporters.
"The UNHCR (U.N. refugee agency) was spending $1 million per day on the refugees, which is ridiculous. These intriguers, all they want is money," Museveni said in his broadside.
"This criminal circus of all sorts of charlatans running around without any serious discussions are one of the problems in Africa," Museveni added.
Museveni said he was pleased to see television pictures of thousands of refugees peacefully trekking back to Rwanda.
"The peasants voted with their feet against a colonial mentality imposed on them by the United Nations and its sister agencies which are not serious and only aim at the money."

Museveni said he recently spoke by telephone to U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata about the refugee problem but she had said nothing could be done because her officers did not have visas for Rwanda.
"One million people may die because of three visas," Museveni said, adding that he had intervened and obtained clearance for the UNHCR staffers directly from Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu.
The UNHCR estimated that 500,000 Hutu refugees were already back home in Rwanda since they started trekking back last week following fighting in eastern Zaire.
